Always returns false in retail -- KCD2's levels contain zero VisAreas/Portals (the CryEngine feature this call tests). Use the `interior` area-label pattern instead (BT `IsInsideAreaWithLabel`, Skald `AreaLabelTrigger`, or `XGenAIModule.IsPointInAreaWithLabelWUID`).

`System.ExecuteConsoleString` is not a Lua ScriptBind function -- it is not callable from Lua at all. To run a console line, cvar assignment, or command from Lua use `System.ExecuteCommand(cmd)`. Separately, the Skald node `wh::conceptmodule::ExecuteConsoleString` exists but is marked Style="Debug" and does not work in the retail game (Modding Tools build only).

Earlier testing concluded this was unusable in any coordinate space; later measurement showed it takes normalised 0..1 coordinates, not pixels -- pixel values render as a huge white shape flying off into the world.
Absent in retail -- calling it has no effect. No filled-polygon drawing is available via System's immediate-mode draw calls.

Documented with a single string-ish signature, but `hud.xml` defines it with 6 parameters (Id, Text, Duration, InDialogue, Priority, Layout) and at least one community mod calls it with 8 (adding ActionHintEnable, OverlayLink). Treat the documented arity as incomplete.
`SetTarget` is not a Soul bind in the retail binary or the runtime dump. The public guide's `soul:SetTarget(nil)` cleanup call does nothing -- it is silently swallowed inside its own pcall.

Do not pass a third argument. The official script_bind docs describe it as a userData value forwarded to the callback, but in game it never arrives, and passing one can stop the timer chain from re-firing.

Pending SetTimerForFunction timers are serialised into the save and re-armed on load. A chain that is actively running (not merely pending) at save time does not carry into the loaded game and is dropped with the old level.

The old context doc claims GetItem returns an opaque proxy table that must be iterated with pairs(). Contradicted by shipped mod code, which reads it.class, it.amount, it.health with plain field indexing.
Treat as a hint, not a walkability oracle: it flipped to false exactly where a runtime-built wall stood, but also returned true for a point measured 40 m underground.

Constant 15.0 on every measured sample (2,343 samples), including fast travel and sleep -- not the old context doc's claim of "spikes to 400+ during time skips, >100 catches all". Use the clock rate (GetWorldTime() delta per real second) to detect skips instead of the ratio value.
